questions.question: A 10 feet long ladder leaning against a wall, reaches the wall at a point 8 feet high. By how much distance should the ladder be moved towards the wall so that its top reaches a point at 9.6 feet high?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial base = √(10² − 8²) = √(100 − 64) = 6 ft

Final base = √(10² − 9.6²) = √(100 − 92.16) = 2.8 ft

Distance moved towards the wall = 6 − 2.8 = 3.2 ft

**∴ The correct answer is 3.2 ft.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac1dcda373f632700269bc048a421d5d2bef70de780a0c5f8b06391f273dac37.png] 

**Given:**

Length of the ladder (Hypotenuse) = 10 ft

Initial height of the wall (Perpendicular₁) = 8 ft

Final height of the wall (Perpendicular₂) = 9.6 ft

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

**Calculations:**

Let the initial distance of the ladder from the wall be x ft.

⇒ 10² = 8² + x²

⇒ 100 = 64 + x²

⇒ x² = 36 ⇒ x = 6 ft

Let the final distance of the ladder from the wall be y ft.

⇒ 10² = 9.6² + y²

⇒ 100 = 92.16 + y²

⇒ y² = 7.84 ⇒ y = 2.8 ft

Distance the ladder moved towards the wall:

⇒ Distance = x − y

⇒ Distance = 6 − 2.8 = 3.2 ft

**∴ The correct answer is 3.2 ft.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers that satisfy the Pythagoras theorem. Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17). The first part of this question directly scales the (3, 4, 5) triplet into (6, 8, 10).

Distance vs Displacement

While the ladder length remains constant, solving for the shifting horizontal and vertical distances requires treating the movement as two completely separate right-angled triangles.

16 men can complete a work in 12 days. 12 women can complete the same work in 32 days. 16 men and 16 women together worked for 4 days, after which the women dropped out and 16 more men joined. In how many days will the men be able to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of work completed by 16 men = 12 days

Number of work completed by 12 women = 32 days

Number of work completed by 16 men and 16 women together = 4 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

According to the question

⇒ 16m × 12 = 12w × 32

⇒ m = 2w

⇒ m/w = 2/1

Efficiency of 1 man = 2 units and Efficiency of 1 woman = 1 unit

Total work = 16m × 12 = (16 × 2 × 12)

⇒ 384 units

Work done by 16 men and 16 women = 4 days

⇒ 16 women = 8 men [1 man = 2 women]

Total men who worked for 4 days = 16 + 8 = 24

So, the amount of work done by 24 men in 4 days = 24 × 2 × 4 = 192 units

Work remaining = (384 – 192) = 192 units

Now, 16 more men joined, so total men = 16 + 16 = 32

Work done by 32 men in 1 day = 32 × 2 = 64 units

The total number of days taken by 32 men to complete the remaining work = 192/64

⇒ 3 days

**∴ The required time to complete the remaining work by men is 3 days**

sum of squares of zero = 21
